text:
Chilly, clear start this morning, right around 40, but it's a decent day. Clouds mix in with some sun, and we climb to near 57 this afternoon. A cold front is sliding through, but the air is so dry that any sprinkle is unlikely to reach Burlington, so I'd leave the umbrella home. Tonight turns clear and cold, down around 31, so expect frost on the windshield first thing.

Tuesday is the sharp turn. Sunshine all day, but high pressure and a north breeze hold us to about 47, roughly 10 degrees cooler than today. Then comes the coldest night of the stretch. Wednesday morning could fall into the teens and 20s, with a record or two possible. The cold doesn't last long. Wednesday afternoon rebounds to the low 50s under sunshine, and Thursday gets into the low 60s before a weak front brings a few light showers late Thursday night.

Wear a real coat Tuesday and Wednesday morning, and cover the tender plants and drain the hoses before Tuesday night.

AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: A cold front will bring light rain showers to portions of northern New York and the higher terrain of Vermont this morning and early this afternoon. Model soundings continue to show a plethora of dry air in the low levels which will likely inhibit much, if not all, rainfall from making it into the deeper valleys. Still, any location that does receive rain today will see well under a tenth of an inch and will only be for a brief period of time. High pressure will quickly build across the region Tuesday with strong cold air advection leading to noticeably cooler temperatures on Tuesday. For example, we will see temperatures warm into the mid 50s to mid 60s today but see temperatures struggle to warm into the mid to upper 40s on Tuesday. Several locations in Vermont have the potential to see record lows Wednesday morning as temperatures fall into the mid teens to lower 20s. This cool down will be short-lived as warm advection will begin on Wednesday and will allow for temperatures to moderate back into the lower 60s by Thursday. KEY MESSAGE 2: With the exception of a few chances for showers Thursday night, mostly dry and seasonably warm weather is expected for late this week into the weekend. Another weak cold front looks to move through the region late Thursday, with the potential for some light rain showers, particularly across northern portions of the forecast area. Heading into the weekend, drier weather looks to prevail, especially for Saturday. Temperatures later this week into the weekend look to be seasonably warm, with daytime high temperatures climbing into the mid 50s and lower 60s and overnight lows falling into the 30s and 40s.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) -Happy Monday! Hopefully you were able to get out and enjoy the lovely weather from this past weekend. For our Monday, there could be a few more clouds and even the chance for a stray passing sprinkle the further north that you are especially right along the Canadian border. The further south you look you stay dry with more sunshine. High temperatures for the day climb into the 50s north, but 60s to about 70 off to the south thanks to that sunshine. Tonight, most of us fall back into the 20s and 30s. Tuesday features more sunshine for all of us, but we do turn a bit cooler, with most climbing into the low and mid 40s for Tuesday afternoon. A cool day is followed by a cool night and most fall back into the teens and 20s for early Wednesday morning. That could be cool enough to even break a record or two. While our Wednesday starts cool, plenty of sunshine through the day will warm us right back into the low and mid 50s for Wednesday afternoon. That is right around where we should be for this time of year. Thursday we look to be even warmer as most climb towards the low and even mid 60s for Thursday afternoon. A few clouds may begin to build in through the day Thursday, and could give way to a few showers Thursday evening into Thursday night. Any rain should be wrapping up by Friday, but we may hang onto a bit more cloud cover through the day Friday with high temperatures in the upper 50s to lower 60s. The weekend forecast at this point is not looking too bad. Saturday for Halloween features nice sunshine with temperatures into the 50s. Trick-or-treat time remains clear as temperatures dip into the 40s and lower 50s. Don’t forget we fall back 1 hour Saturday night into Sunday.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-10-25T21:18:00Z — same caveat): More clouds Monday, few light showers possible near the Canadian border — Clouds increase tonight, and it will be seasonably cold with patchy frost. Lows will be near 40 in the Champlain Valley, but most towns fall to the upper 20s and 30s. After some early rays of sun, Monday turns mostly cloudy with a few spot showers in northern areas, due to a cold front on approach. Highs reach the upper 50s there. Southern Vermont looks brighter overall, where highs again push well into the 60s. Behind that front, a shot of unseasonable cold arrives Tuesday, as highs fall back to the mid-40s. Expect a mostly sunny sky, with a noticeable north breeze. Wednesday starts with another widespread freeze, but it turns seasonable by afternoon, with highs in the low 50s and a mostly sunny sky. Another warmup arrives late week with highs in the 60s, thanks to a gusty south breeze. A few showers are likely Thursday night into Friday, with another cold front on approach, though not anticipating any significant rain. Halloween weekend looks dry and seasonable, with a mix of sun and clouds. Highs reach the low 60s.
